title: hidden-kernel-regression-probe-suite-2026
author: Asha Patel
summary: This document defines a small, repeatable probe suite designed to detect 'hidden' kernel regressions that do not show up in standard throughput or latency benchmarks but cause tail anomalies, degraded concurrency profiles, or resource jitter under specific sequences of requests. It provides probe definitions, execution matrices, expected telemetry signatures, validation criteria, and an operational runbook for investigating incidents triggered by the suite.
scope: Applies to kernel and scheduler changes in the serving runtime, the CI/CD performance gate, nightly regression scans, and on-call incident triage. Not intended for end-user workload benchmarking; focused on micro-patterns that expose correctness, contention, and subtle performance regressions at the kernel/scheduler boundary.
background: During 2025 we observed multiple regressions that escaped standard microbenchmarks but surfaced as 99.9th-percentile spikes or rare failed hedges in production. Root causes included subtle preemption ordering changes, KV-cache warmup races, and kernel selection edge-cases for mixed attention layers. This probe suite codifies the lessons into automated checks and operator guidance.
probe-suite-overview: The suite is intentionally compact (12 probes) and orthogonal: each probe targets one hypothesis (e.g., preemption contention, kvcache starvation, priority inversion). Probes are categorized as: 1) concurrency stressors, 2) sequence-sensitive traces, 3) long-tail generator patterns, 4) fallback/variant oscillation stimulants. Each probe yields a reproducible execution trace, an expected kernel-selection histogram, and a set of telemetry assertions.
experimental-profiles:
Table: probe matrix (columns: probe_id | intent | runtime inputs | concurrency shape | expected telemetry signature | fail threshold)

1 | PK-CONTEND | small prompt + rapid follow-ups | 32 concurrent sessions (burst 128 qps) | kernel-select spread > 1.5x baseline, queued-ops > 25ms | fail if 99th latency > baseline*2 or kernel churn > baseline*1.8
2 | KV-STARVE | interleaved long/short sequences to evict KV | mixed lengths (16/1024 tokens) per session | increased cold-kv misses and kv-eviction events | fail if kv-miss-rate delta > 5%
3 | PREEMPT-RACE | adversarial task preemption pattern | 8 high-priority + 64 low-priority streams | preemption-count spike, CPU/SM scheduling gaps | fail if preemptions increase > 3x and tail latency > baseline*2
4 | FAILBACK-OSC | model variant fallback oscillation | fluctuating capacity with model switch allowed | repeated model swap events; oscillation >= 3 switches/min | fail on repeated swap loops causing >5% request failures
5 | ATTENTION-SHARD | strided attention shapes that hit sharding limits | unusual seq len (2048) with tiled inputs | kernel memory allocation spikes, fragmentation | fail if OOM-retries > 0 or memory-fragmentation increases > 10%
6 | GRPC-REROUTE | connection reuse with pipelined requests | long lived gRPC streams with interleaving | connection-reset / pipeline regeneration events | fail if connection-reset rate > 0.1%
7 | LATENCY-AMPLIFY | small sequential deltas that accumulate | many small tokens with jittered arrival | amplified tail around 99.99th | fail if amplification factor > 2x
8 | BATCH-SLICE | batch slicing under preemption | high batch sizes with frequent preemption | dropped/partially-processed batches | fail if dropped-batch rate > 0.05%
9 | KV-WARMUP | cold-start warmup with diverse keys | first-request heavy, then stable | slow warming curve for KV hit-rate | fail if warmup > expected window by 2x
10 | MEMORY-STEER | memory compaction interaction | allocation/free churn microbursts | fragmentation compaction events | fail if compaction latency > 50ms
11 | QUANT-SNAP | quantized-kernel path divergence | mixed model variants, different quant levels | kernel-path split; unexpected precision regressions | fail if output-norm dev > threshold
12 | TRACE-EMIT | synthetic trace that exercises trace annotations | high cardinality decision traces | trace loss or mis-annotation | fail if trace-drop > 0.5%
runbook: 1) Run probe suite on staging cluster using the harness (see sample-commands). 2) If any probe fails, gather the following artifacts: kernel selection histograms, compact trace for the failed window, per-GPU occupancy reports, kvcache hit-rate time series, and preemption counters. 3) Create an incident with label 'probe-regression' and attach artifacts. 4) Triage: a) check kernel code rollouts in the last 24 hours; b) reproduce locally with the kernel debug build; c) run delta-probes (narrower inputs) to isolate minimal reproducer. 5) If the regression reproduces locally, bisect kernel changes using the autotest harness. 6) If not reproducible locally, escalate to runtime/platform owners and request a sampled prod replay under controlled traffic. 7) After fix, add a targeted microtest to the CI gate and mark the probe as having a baseline update. 8) Document root cause and add remediation guidance to the knowledge base.
sample-commands:
# Run full suite (k8s staging)
export STAGING_CLUSTER=staging-runtime
kubectl exec -it probe-harness -- /opt/probe/run-suite.sh --suite hidden-kernel-regressions --concurrency 64 --duration 30m

# Run a single probe locally (container)
docker run --rm -e PROBE=PK-CONTEND gcr.io/redwood/probe-harness:2026-02 /bin/bash -c "/opt/probe/run-probe --id PK-CONTEND --samples 10000"

# Collect artifacts (example)
/opt/tools/collect-telemetry --start 2026-03-01T10:00:00Z --end 2026-03-01T10:30:00Z --selectors kernel_histogram,kvcache,preemption,occupancy --out /tmp/probe-artifacts.tgz
telemetry-queries:
PromQL examples to detect probe signatures:
1) Kernel churn (per-minute): sum(rate(kernel_select_events_total[1m])) by (kernel) / sum(rate(kernel_select_events_total[1m]))
2) KV miss delta (windowed): (rate(kv_cache_miss_total[5m]) - rate(kv_cache_miss_total[1h])) / rate(kv_cache_miss_total[1h])
3) Preemption spike: increase(preemption_count_total[5m]) > 3 * increase(preemption_count_total[1h])
4) Trace loss: rate(trace_dropped_total[5m]) / rate(trace_emitted_total[5m]) > 0.005
expected-signatures: Kernel-selection histograms should remain within 10% of nightly baseline for stable probes
KV miss-rate increases over probe window indicate starvation behavior
Preemption spikes correlate with increased 99.9th latency and queued op durations
Oscillatory model swaps will manifest as repeated model_switch events with no net capacity change
incident-triage-checklist:
- Confirm probe parameters (seed, concurrency, duration) match the failing run
- Attach artifacts to incident (kernel histograms, compact traces, occupancy)
- Identify whether the signal is deterministic or probabilistic (run the probe 10x)
- Cross-check recent rollouts: kernel, scheduler policy, model-variant-mapper
- Reproduce against debug build with extended tracing
- If reproduction fails: request sampled prod replay (timeboxed)
- If reproduction succeeds: run git-bisect on kernel commits and mark candidate commit
- Patch, run probes, and submit fix with perf regression note
